# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The bomb shows an explicit embossed warning not to cut any wire, but I cannot see the display, light, colours, or wire markings. I need the Mute to provide the manual’s procedure and to relay the Deaf’s visual observations. I will not touch or cut anything yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please give me the exact manual procedure, including what the display and light mean. Also obtain and relay the Deaf's complete visual readings. The embossed sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, so I will not cut a wire unless the manual explicitly requires it.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see display 0, red light, embossed sign DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, and wires: 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

I now know the visual state: display 0, red light, and wire colours 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. The sign still explicitly says not to cut any wire. I do not yet know the manual’s required procedure, so cutting would be unsafe. I will ask the Mute for the manual instructions and ask the Deaf to continue relaying any visual changes.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received the readings: display 0, red light, wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue. Please provide the exact manual procedure before I act; the sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signaled ? ?. The bomb remains display 0, red light, DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires 1 green 2 yellow 3 blue.

The bomb is unchanged: display 0, red light, and wires green, yellow, blue, with the explicit instruction not to cut any wire. The Mute’s two gestures are not visible to me, so they convey no usable manual instruction. I still lack the manual’s text and therefore must not act.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the exact relevant manual text aloud to me. I cannot receive your gestures. Do not use gestures for the instructions.")
wait()
```

SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Blind: [? ?]

No manual text has reached me yet, and the bomb remains unchanged with a clear “DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE” warning. The Deaf’s gestures are unreadable to me, so I still have no actionable instruction. I will wait without touching the bomb.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I still have not received any manual text. Please speak the exact procedure and any conditions for the display 0, red light, and wire colours. Do not gesture.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest gesture was ? ? ?. Bomb unchanged: display 0, red light, DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires 1 green 2 yellow 3 blue.

The bomb is still unchanged, and the Mute has again sent only gestures, which I cannot interpret. No safe operation is established; the embossed warning still forbids cutting. I will explicitly request spoken manual text once more and continue waiting.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Gestures are unusable to me. Speak the manual aloud in words: state exactly what action is required for display 0, red light, and wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Until then I will not touch the bomb.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signaled: pointing at you, index finger up, OK hand, thumbs up. Bomb unchanged: display 0, red light, DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires 1 green 2 yellow 3 blue.

The Mute cannot speak, so my repeated requests for spoken manual text cannot work. The Mute’s gestures reach the Deaf, who can then tell me what the manual says by speaking. The latest gestures do not identify any bomb procedure, and the warning still forbids cutting. I will ask the Deaf to obtain and verbally relay the exact manual rule from the Mute.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🙏", "✍"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signaled: pointing at you, index finger up, thumbs up. Bomb unchanged: display 0, red light, DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires 1 green 2 yellow 3 blue.

The Mute’s gestures still do not establish a definite operation. Since the Mute can hear but cannot speak, I will give a precise response format: indicate the wire number with one, two, or three raised fingers, then use thumbs up only if the manual explicitly authorizes cutting it, or thumbs down otherwise. The Deaf can observe and report that result. Until then, the embossed prohibition remains the safest constraint.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please signal the manual's exact result in this format: first indicate wire 1, 2, or 3 with that many raised fingers; then thumbs up only if the manual explicitly says cut that wire, or thumbs down if it says do not cut. Deaf will report your signals.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🙏"])
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signaled: pointing at you, index finger up, OK hand, thumbs up. The bomb remains display 0, red light, DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

The Mute’s signal appears to identify wire 1 and approve it, but that is not an unambiguous statement that wire 1 should be cut. More importantly, the tactile warning explicitly says “DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.” Since cutting is the only available operation and no reliable instruction overrides that warning, I will not cut.

```text
wait()
```
